findings.title: Grant shortcut check in isAccessTokenId is inverted and uses the wrong offsets
findings.body: The grant shortcut sits at chars 4-5 of the 6-char prefix, so `substring(4, 6)` is the right slice. This code takes `substring(3, 5)`, which spans the token-type and grant characters. It also returns false when the slice equals the expected shortcut. The inversion and the wrong offset hide each other, so the matcher accepts a token whose grant shortcut is wrong. It would reject the correct one only in the unlikely case that the shifted slice equals the shortcut. The tests therefore don't check the grant type they claim to check. Fix: compare `substring(4, 6)` and return false when it is not equal to the expected shortcut.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId actually checks grantType
findings.body: The `requireNonNull` call on line 73 passes `grantType` but its message says rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is accepted, and `encodeTokenId` would then produce an ID ending in 'null'. Check `rawTokenId` instead.
